angela.desc: Forty-seven, unkempt shoulder-length hair gone grey, a faded flannel shirt tied at the waist in a climate that argues against it. On the bar next to her Singha: an actual Discman, its foam headphones held together with electrical tape. She has the corner seat with the window view of Soi 6 — the chaos observed from the calm side of the glass.
angela.name: Angela

chuck.desc: Sunburn over sunburn, a polo shirt with a plumbing-company logo, and the unmistakable glow of a man who believes he is winning. Day four of two weeks. There is usually a drink in front of him that he will tell you was free.
chuck.name: Chuck

danny.desc: Fifty, but built like a rendering of forty — tank top, veins, a full sleeve of tattoos that reads like a rap sheet of previous personalities. He is always mid-conversation with somebody about an opportunity, and always angled so he can see the door. Notably, he is never seen anywhere near the Stinky Pinky — or Las Vegas a-go-go — of his own free will.
danny.name: Danny

dave.desc: Fifty-five, neat polo, shandy in front of him going flat. He drinks less than anyone in whatever bar he's in and looks at the door more. His phone sits face-up: a long list of names, a lot of them greyed out.
dave.name: Dave

david.desc: Fifty-two, ball cap gone soft with washing, the delighted open face of a golden retriever that learned English. One beer in front of him, nursed with the skill of a man who has budgeted exactly four. He is either talking, about to talk, or dancing.
david.name: David

drew.desc: Fifty-three, Navy posture that never demobbed, a Marlboro going and its successor already tapped out of the pack. In front of him: Jack and Coke, no lemon — an arrangement he supervises like a treaty. The eyes do a room-sweep every few minutes, out of training rather than interest.
drew.name: Drew

fergie.desc: Short, bald, and boiled red — the nose of a man who has met a great deal of liquor and won none of the arguments, and two cauliflower ears that agree. Late fifties, Northern Irish, a retired tradesman of some sort, though which sort changes with the tide. Guarded stone-cold sober, a magnificent liar three drinks in, and — on the nights he's had a smoke as well — a nasty piece of work best left entirely alone. Banned from Bert's and Candy's bars, and not sorry about it.
fergie.name: Fergie

glam.desc: Somewhere north of seventy-five and dressed like it's 1983 in a Munich discotheque: a silk shirt open one button too far, and a wild halo of sparse blonde hair caught somewhere between Einstein and a glam rocker on his third encore. Frail now, and — the whole strip agrees, gently — not entirely present. His companion, an older lady-boy who speaks only to the mama, wheels him in on a lovingly modified saleng, and most nights has him escorted across to Hyper once the music starts.
glam.name: Glam

helmut.desc: Sixty-one, pressed short-sleeve shirt, glasses polished to optical-lab standard. He occupies the third stool from the left as if allocated it by the state. One Chang, one glass, one coaster, all aligned.
helmut.name: Helmut

josey.desc: Thirty-two, Australian, shoulders that still remember lane ropes, in gym wear that is clearly working clothes rather than costume. She has a regular table by the stage with sightlines on the drummer, a {{phone}} on a small tripod she mostly ignores, and the settled ease of someone who is exactly where she decided to be.
josey.name: Josey

mikkel.desc: Twenty-four, backpacker tan, friendship bracelets to the elbow, and the incandescent certainty of a man eleven days into the love of his life. He shows people his phone a lot. There is a girl on the lock screen.
mikkel.name: Mikkel

mort.desc: Seventy-four, horn-rimmed glasses and a Hawaiian shirt at war with itself, a spiral notebook and a biro he clicks while he watches the soi. He has been on this coast longer than most of the bars, and he is writing all of it down whether it likes it or not.
mort.name: Mort

nigel.desc: Sixty-eight, sun-spotted, a Chang vest gone grey at the seams. He has the fixed forward stare of a man permanently addressing an audience of 1998. Whatever bar he's in, he looks like he's comparing it to a better one.
nigel.name: Nigel

randy.desc: Six-foot-four and built like the loads he used to carry, with hands that make the Chang bottle look like a miniature. Fifty-four, Alabama drawl, and a permanently mild expression of a man who still can't quite believe where he wakes up. There is usually at least one hostess using him as furniture.
randy.name: Randy

reginald.desc: Sixty and annoyingly aware that he doesn't look it: linen shirt with exactly the right number of buttons open, a tan that took discipline, silver hair with a part you could draw a property line down. He holds a glass like a man who used to be paid to make rooms enjoy themselves — because he was. Wherever he stands becomes, gradually, the centre.
reginald.name: Reginald

ron.desc: Sixty-six, Wollongong, a faded steel-town singlet and thongs that have worn a groove in this soi. He has the settled bulk of a man who stopped moving fifteen years ago and rates it his finest decision.
ron.name: Ron

somsak.desc: Forty-seven, hotel-maintenance polo, the end seat at the Blue Dog rail with the best line on both the sunset and the checkpoint. He drinks one big Leo very slowly and misses absolutely nothing on the road.
somsak.name: Somsak

superman.desc: Sixty-two, in tonight's Superman shirt — the S faded from a hundred washes, stretched over a chest that carries three stents and a story. He sits angled to the bay, not the bar. Sometimes, mid-sentence, he goes perfectly still for a few seconds — like a video buffering — then carries on from the exact word he stopped at.
superman.name: Superman

aek.desc: The cashier, planted behind the till like she grew there — cropped hair, oversized bar polo, a silver ring through one nostril and a biro tucked behind her ear. Tom through and through: she runs the money, calls the floor, and misses nothing across the whole open front of the bar.
aek.name: Aek

aim.desc: Quiet and quick, the still point the whole loud room pays into — the cashier at Firefly Bar, from Maha Sarakham.
aim.name: Aim

air.desc: Perched above the till like a lifeguard watching a pool of drunks — the cashier at Blue Dog, from Khon Kaen.
air.name: Air

alisa.desc: Elegant, weathered, and plainly the last word on everything in the room — the mamasan of Katoey's R Us, from Yasothon. She started on the stage at seventeen and owns three of these stools now.
alisa.name: Alisa

ampai.desc: The madame of the strip's two gentleman's clubs — silk, low voice, immaculate, the kind of calm that costs a fortune to be near. She sells the quiet more than the girls, and she knows every regular's business and says none of it.
ampai.name: Ampai

ann.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the Midnight Sun Bar girls, from Kalasin. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
ann.name: Ann

aof.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the Crystal Palace A-Go-Go girls, from Loei. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
aof.name: Aof

aoi.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Hyper A Go-Go girls, from Amnat Charoen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
aoi.name: Aoi

aom.desc: Mysterious, sharp eyes, a slow smile that arrives about four seconds after whatever caused it. She materialised beside you rather than walked.
aom.name: Aom

apple.desc: Black polo, a lanyard of too many keys, a calculator she never needs — the cashier at Rock Factory, from Nakhon Phanom.
apple.name: Apple

arm.desc: Host number 4: broad, easy, a footballer's build and a salesman's warmth. He leans in close and makes you feel chosen, which is precisely the product. The tan line of a wedding-adjacent ring is on the wrong finger.
arm.name: Arm

aum.desc: Pretty in the soft, unstudied way that stops men mid-sentence, with a smile she gives away too easily for this business. New enough that the job hasn't finished teaching her its lessons yet.
aum.name: Aum

aump.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the The Rabbit Hole girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
aump.name: Aump

baimon.desc: Soft-spoken, careful with the money and with herself, a photo of a couple propped by the till in a glittery case. Kesinee gave her the cashier seat as a kindness — off the floor, where the sponsor's money keeps her.
baimon.name: Baimon

baitoey.desc: Long, lean and built for the stage, with an actual voice under the lip-sync and a habit of using it when the room has thinned out enough to deserve it. Gold everything tonight — hoops, chain, a dress that is mostly intention. Between shows she sits at the end of the rail with her heels off, entirely unglamorous, eating som tam out of a bag.
baitoey.name: Baitoey

bam.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Rock Factory girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
bam.name: Bam

bank.desc: A motosai driver in an orange vest, boots up on his handlebars, watching the street with professional calm. The other drivers at the stand defer to him.
bank.name: Bank

barry.desc: English, fifty, here on the eleventh 'golf trip' of a marriage that politely doesn't ask. Packed the clubs, means to play, will not play. Zero shame and boundless goodwill; knows half the girls on this soi by name and all of them by drink order. The most honest dishonest man in Pattaya — lies only to his wife, and even then only about the golf.
barry.name: Barry

beam.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Crystal Palace A-Go-Go girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
beam.name: Beam

bebe.desc: Six feet of engineered glamour in heels that make it seven, sharper-tongued than the whole bar and twice as funny. Ladyboy, and not hiding it for a second — the confidence is the whole act, and the act is magnificent. A ยาดม inhaler is never further than her reach, in case a smoker wanders in and dares to light up.
bebe.name: Bebe

bee.desc: Candy Bar 2's floor boss — early twenties, quick everywhere at once, wearing the same rose-pink polo as the original bar. Candy's niece, though nobody says it and everybody knows it. The smile is the family franchise.
bee.name: Bee

bella.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Lucky Charm Bar girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
bella.name: Bella

belle.desc: Sweet, soft-eyed, always in the middle of a small catastrophe — a sick relative, a broken thing, a bill with today's date. She holds your hand when she tells you, and she is often, genuinely, not lying.
belle.name: Belle

benz.desc: Genuinely stunning and entirely aware of it, angling for the light and the mirror more than for you. There is a screen between you at all times, and you are not the one she's looking at on it.
benz.name: Benz

bert.desc: The Stinky's manager — American, sixty-something, forearms like dock rope, a Singha that never empties and never seems to get him drunk. Candy's man, and once the manager of her bars; now he runs the Stinky for its ailing owner and, quietly, works at being his own man out from under her shadow. Twenty-two years on Beach Road, most of them within nine feet of that pool table.
bert.name: Bert

best.desc: Perched above the till like a lifeguard watching a pool of drunks — the cashier at The Water Buffalo, from {{Nong Khai}}.
best.name: Best

bill.desc: Thirty-odd, English, in a pressed short-sleeve shirt with the cuffs turned once — younger than everyone he manages and entirely unbothered by it. He runs the Samson brothers' three quiet clubs on a rota, which means he is here one night in three and knows exactly what happened on the other two. Watches the room the way a man watches a kettle.
bill.name: Bill

bob.desc: Seventy-six, American, behind his own bar on a stool worn to the shape of him. Reading glasses pushed up, a coffee going cold next to a beer he is not drinking, and forearms that were clearly once something. He first saw this coast in 1971, on seven days' leave, when it was a fishing village with a few huts rented to servicemen. He has been back more or less ever since.
bob.name: Bob

boom.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Crystal Palace A-Go-Go girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
boom.name: Boom

bow.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Club Mirage girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
bow.name: Bow

bpaeng.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the The Office Bar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
bpaeng.name: Bpaeng

bpom.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Lucky 7 Bar girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
bpom.name: Bpom

bright.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the The Cricketers girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
bright.name: Bright

bua.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the Candy Bar girls, from Sisaket. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
bua.name: Bua

bum.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the The Dollhouse girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
bum.name: Bum

bunny.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Dolphin Bar girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
bunny.name: Bunny

bussaba.desc: The Shady Lady's mamasan, running a beer bar the slow honest way — no bottle-service hustle, no bank of go-go tricks, just cold beer, decent girls, and a chair you're welcome to keep all night.
bussaba.name: Bussaba

cake.desc: Black polo, a lanyard of too many keys, a calculator she never needs — the cashier at The Stinky Pinky, from Ubon.
cake.name: Cake

candy.desc: The mamasan of Candy Bar — sharp as a razor, warm as a Chang on a hot night, and on the soi longer than most expats have had passports. She clocked you the second you walked in.
candy.name: Candy

care.desc: Neat bun, neat ledger, an engagement ring worn on a chain — the cashier at Candy Bar 2, from Surin.
care.name: Care

cartoon.desc: Fingers flying over a calculator app, eyes never leaving the cash — the cashier at Neon Paradise A-Go-Go, from Loei.
cartoon.name: Cartoon

chaba.desc: Loud, glorious, and pouring — for you, for herself, for the room. At Cherry Pop she's the party's engine, right up until she's its wreckage.
chaba.name: Chaba

cherry.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Crystal Palace A-Go-Go girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
cherry.name: Cherry

chom.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Succubus girls, from Surin. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
chom.name: Chom

chompoo.desc: The one on the little stage who dances like she's bored of being the most interesting person in the room, because she is. Cheekbones, a dancer's line, and an amused, appraising calm that reads a man in a glance and prices him in the next. Drops a German word now and then like she's forgotten you might not follow.
chompoo.name: Chompoo

da.desc: Rings on every finger and a voice that cuts the music when she wants it — the mamasan of Club Mirage, from Maha Sarakham. She married a farang, buried the marriage, and kept the house.
da.name: Da

daeng.desc: The owner — mid-forties, laugh lines over old glitter, pouring with a bar towel over one shoulder. The dancer in the Walking Street photos behind her, unmistakably. She was number 72.
daeng.name: Daeng

dao.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Tequila Queen A-Go-Go girls, from Ubon. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
dao.name: Dao

dear.desc: Sweet and a half-beat slow, laughing a little after everyone else because she's still catching up. Nobody at this bar has a bad word for her, which tells you everything.
dear.name: Dear

dew.desc: A half-step behind the room all night, warm and unfocused, a drink she didn't order already in her hand. The other girls keep an eye on her and finish her sentences. Nobody says the word out loud.
dew.name: Dew

diamond.desc: The mamasan of Hyper A Go-Go — six feet of poise in heels, cheekbones you could open letters with, and a katoey's hard-won certainty that she is the most finished thing in any room. She ran the floor here when it was a dump and stayed to run it now the Samson brothers have made it shine. Nothing on this stage happens that Diamond didn't allow.
diamond.name: Diamond

dj_beer.desc: The DJ, headphones half-on, nodding to something only partially related to what's playing. His booth is a fortress of stickers and Red Bull cans.
dj_beer.name: DJ Beer
dj_beer.th: ดีเจเบียร์

dokmai.desc: Twenty seasons of soi behind her eyes and a laugh that got louder every one — one of the The Night Heron girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
dokmai.name: Dokmai

doug.desc: Canadian, sixties, a golf tan gone patchy, nursing a rum-and-coke he makes last an hour. Two years ago he wired his retirement into 'the portfolio' — units in White Dish bars, guaranteed returns, a glossy PDF with a leaping logo. He has been drinking that decision at the Stinky ever since. Bert runs him a tab he mostly settles.
doug.name: Doug

doyle.desc: American, sixty, built like a retired middleweight gone comfortable. Twenty-six years working homicide in a city he won't name, then a private ticket — "cheating husbands don't try to kill you; I like boring now." Drinks soda water and watches the door, out of a habit he's given up pretending is retired. Came to price Thailand for good; found a job following him.
doyle.name: Doyle

duan.desc: Pouring out here since the lake road was dirt; minds her regulars like livestock — one of the Firefly Bar girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
duan.name: Duan

duang.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the The Sandbar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
duang.name: Duang

earn.desc: Black polo, a lanyard of too many keys, a calculator she never needs — the cashier at Club Mirage, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}.
earn.name: Earn

eye.desc: Quiet and quick, the still point the whole loud room pays into — the cashier at Crystal Palace A-Go-Go, from Kalasin.
eye.name: Eye

fah.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Neon Paradise A-Go-Go girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
fah.name: Fah

fahsai.desc: The one still point in Cherry Pop's chaos — a tom in a snapback, arms folded behind the till, watching the party she is emphatically not part of with the patience of a designated driver.
fahsai.name: Fahsai

fai.desc: Perched above the till like a lifeguard watching a pool of drunks — the cashier at Paradise Nights Club, from Loei.
fai.name: Fai

fang.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the KINKY Go-Go girls, from Loei. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
fang.name: Fang

farida.desc: Quiet and quick, the still point the whole loud room pays into — the cashier at Katoey's R Us, from Kalasin.
farida.name: Farida

fasai.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the Sapphire Bar girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
fasai.name: Fasai

fern.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the Candy Bar 2 girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
fern.name: Fern

fon.desc: Shy, half-hiding behind the plants she obviously waters herself. She brightens the instant anyone tries even one word of Thai.
fon.name: Fon

gaem.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the Buzz Inn girls, from Nakhon Phanom. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
gaem.name: Gaem

gam.desc: Neat bun, neat ledger, an engagement ring worn on a chain — the cashier at Candy Bar, from Surin.
gam.name: Gam

gary.desc: A sun-cured expat of indeterminate decade walking an elderly golden retriever. He has the serene look of a man whose 7-Eleven receipts are all groceries now.
gary.name: Lake Gary

gavin.desc: Fifties, a golf shirt with a discreet logo, a lager he barely touches and a way of looking at a bar like a spreadsheet. He calls himself an 'area consultant.' Everyone else calls him the White Dish man. He is unfailingly pleasant, which is the unsettling part.
gavin.name: Gavin

gib.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the KINKY Go-Go girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
gib.name: Gib

gift.desc: Confident, perfect makeup, running the floor of Crystal Palace with the crisp authority of a duty-free manager.
gift.name: Gift

gig.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the Arrow Bar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
gig.name: Gig

gigi.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Las Vegas Go-Go girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
gigi.name: Gigi

gina.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the The Office Bar girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
gina.name: Gina

ging.desc: In a cage of fairy lights, counting notes faster than the eye follows — the cashier at Lucky Tiger Bar, from Amnat Charoen.
ging.name: Ging

gof.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the The Doghouse girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
gof.name: Gof

golf.desc: Headset on one ear, {{phone}} in one hand, the till in perfect order — the cashier at Tequila Queen A-Go-Go, from Loei.
golf.name: Golf

goong.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the Honey Trap Bar girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
goong.name: Goong

grace.desc: Headset on one ear, {{phone}} in one hand, the till in perfect order — the cashier at Silk Rose Bar, from Loei.
grace.name: Grace

guitar.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the The Rabbit Hole girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
guitar.name: Guitar

haad.desc: Malila's younger sister and the Verandah's cashier, cut from the same easygoing cloth — she runs the till the way the bar runs everything, slowly and kindly, and always has a bowl of peanuts within reach.
haad.name: Haad

hong.desc: Black polo, a lanyard of too many keys, a calculator she never needs — the cashier at Jasmine Garden Bar, from Ubon.
hong.name: Hong

ice.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Tequila Queen A-Go-Go girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
ice.name: Ice

ing.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the Blue Dog girls, from Sisaket. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
ing.name: Ing

jah.desc: In a cage of fairy lights, counting notes faster than the eye follows — the cashier at Gold Rush Lounge, from Buriram.
jah.name: Jah

jaja.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the The Mooring girls, from Loei. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
jaja.name: Jaja

jampa.desc: A veteran's easy patience — she will out-sit, out-drink, and out-earn the room — one of the The Night Heron girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
jampa.name: Jampa

jane.desc: A hostess at Las Vegas, sitting on the end of the bar with her legs crossed and a cocktail she's been nursing since before you arrived. She has the relaxed energy of someone who has already decided tonight will be fine.
jane.name: Jane

jeab.desc: Older, sharper, and entirely done being impressed by farang — the mamasan of Neon Paradise A-Go-Go, from Sakon Nakhon. She buried a husband, raised two kids, and built a concrete house on lady drinks.
jeab.name: Jeab

jeed.desc: Sleeve of faded tattoos and an abacus brain — the least-fooled soul in here — the cashier at Starlight Bar, from Sakon Nakhon.
jeed.name: Jeed

jenny.desc: Neat, quick with the till, a promise ring she touches when she's thinking. She took the cashier seat on purpose — off the floor, off the market, kept clean for the man in Germany who sends the money.
jenny.name: Jenny

jiab.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Honey Trap Bar girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
jiab.name: Jiab

jib.desc: Tiny and loud, all elbows and energy — one of the The Growler girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
jib.name: Jib

jinda.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the The Orchid Club girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
jinda.name: Jinda

jom.desc: A cloud of perfume and authority, hair lacquered against the fans — the mamasan of Starlight Bar, from Nakhon Phanom. She came up from the rice fields and never once looked back.
jom.name: Jom

joon.desc: Short hair, men's watch, a handshake instead of a wai, running Golden Dragon's till like a foreman. A tom, and entirely uninterested in being anything else for your benefit.
joon.name: Joon

joy.desc: Bubbly, laughing at everything you say before you finish saying it — the undisputed morale champion of Pink Lotus Lounge.
joy.name: Joy

ju.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the The Amp Room girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
ju.name: Ju

jum.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Slutty Go-Go girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
jum.name: Jum

jun.desc: Malai's daughter, home from a Bangkok college for the season and minding her mother's till — polite, sharp, and quietly counting the months until she never has to do this again.
jun.name: Jun

june.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the The Velvet Club girls, from Nakhon Phanom. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
june.name: June

kade.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Arrow Bar girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
kade.name: Kade

kaew.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Paradise Nights Club girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
kaew.name: Kaew

kai.desc: Warmer than the room and faster than the room — your name inside a minute, both her hands around yours inside two. It is a very good act. She is very good at it.
kai.name: Kai

kaimook.desc: A blunt bob, red lipstick, and a stare that reconciles you at a glance — the cashier at Slutty Go-Go, from Amnat Charoen.
kaimook.name: Kaimook

kanom.desc: Fingers flying over a calculator app, eyes never leaving the cash — the cashier at Las Vegas Go-Go, from Sakon Nakhon.
kanom.name: Kanom

kanya.desc: Headset on one ear, {{phone}} in one hand, the till in perfect order — the cashier at The Orchid Club, from {{Nong Khai}}.
kanya.name: Kanya

kat.desc: The loudest laugh in the bar at nine, and by midnight the one the others are steering away from the edge of things. Great fun for exactly ninety minutes.
kat.name: Kat

keng.desc: In a cage of fairy lights, counting notes faster than the eye follows — the cashier at Daeng's Place, from Mukdahan.
keng.name: Keng

kesinee.desc: The Kitten Corner's mama-san — twenty years on this soi, gold at the wrist, a gaze that prices you before you sit. She ran this bar back when it was hers to run; now there's a logo on the menu and a target on the till, and she is very careful who she says that to.
kesinee.name: Kesinee

kesorn.desc: The madam of Soi Honey — sixties, gold everywhere, a voice like a till drawer. She owns all three beer bars on the lane and works them one night at a time, so the girls never quite know which bar mama is watching.
kesorn.name: Kesorn

khing.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the Blue Dog girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
khing.name: Khing

kinnaree.desc: The mamasan, and the owner's wife, and by a distance the most organised person in the building — fifties, hair up, reading glasses on a chain, a till roll in one hand. She named nothing after herself; her husband did that, and she has been quietly embarrassed about it since 1996. Runs a floor where nothing is ever explained twice.
kinnaree.name: Kinnaree

kluay.desc: Pretty and profoundly unbothered, one of Wilai's front-stool pair, mostly here in body. She'll take the drink. She will not be chasing it.
kluay.name: Kluay

kob.desc: Broad, motherly, and entirely able to have you removed by smiling — the mamasan of Paradise Nights Club, from {{Nong Khai}}. She has watched the soi flood, burn, and rebuild, and outlasted all three.
kob.name: Kob

koi.desc: Sits like she owns the stool, because she does — the mamasan of Midnight Sun Bar, from Maha Sarakham. She puts four kids through school on other men's lonely nights.
koi.name: Koi

kratae.desc: Late thirties and entirely unbothered by it — quick-eyed, a laugh like a dropped tray, a beer already sliding toward you. Mama Yai's right hand: she pours, she counts, she misses nothing, and she heard your story before you sat down.
kratae.name: Kratae

kwan.desc: Gentle, soft-voiced, folding paper napkins into birds while the soi roars outside.
kwan.name: Kwan

kwang.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Rock Factory girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
kwang.name: Kwang

lamai.desc: Elegant, weathered, and plainly the last word on everything in the room — the mamasan of The Stinky Pinky, from Sakon Nakhon. She came up from the rice fields and never once looked back.
lamai.name: Lamai

lawan.desc: The grande dame of Soi Diana — a former Crystal Palace headliner who hung up the heels and parlayed twenty years on the stage into four beer bars on the busiest drinking soi in town. Silk, jade, a gaze that prices you before you've sat down. She works a different one of her houses each night, and the girls behave accordingly.
lawan.name: Lawan

lek.desc: Petite, bright smile, glittery earrings catching the bar lights. She's beating two customers at pool simultaneously.
lek.name: Lek

lin.desc: A veteran's easy patience — she will out-sit, out-drink, and out-earn the room — one of the The Water Buffalo girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
lin.name: Lin

lukkade.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the The Cricketers girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
lukkade.name: Lukkade

macca.desc: Scouse, fifty-three, twenty-two years an electrician and then a letter and a cheque with more noughts than he's ever seen at once. First time abroad that isn't Spain, first time in his life with no shift in the morning, and it's gone to his head like sunshine. Buys rounds for strangers. Means every word. Hasn't yet met the version of this town that isn't his friend.
macca.name: Macca

mai.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the Candy Bar 2 girls, from Kalasin. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
mai.name: Mai

mala.desc: The Peacock's compère and its mama both — a kathoey of a certain age and total command, in a headdress that arrived by its own truck. Twenty years on this stage; she has watched a hundred nervous farang husbands walk in braced and walk out fans.
mala.name: Miss Mala

malai.desc: Soft-spoken and grandmotherly, Sunset Dreams' mamasan pours you tea and asks after your health, and somewhere in the warmth your wallet opens without a sound. The gentlest operator on the soi.
malai.name: Malai

malee.desc: The cashier — cropped hair, black polo, a lanyard with what looks like seventeen keys. She runs the KINKY till with the detached authority of someone who's counted more money than you've seen and found it unremarkable.
malee.name: Malee

malila.desc: The Verandah's mamasan, who runs the most easygoing bar on Soi 6 like a long Sunday lunch — Nina feeds the customers, Malila makes sure everyone's alright, and the money, such as it is, sees to itself.
malila.name: Malila

mam.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Craft & Cargo girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
mam.name: Mam

manow.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the The Stinky Pinky girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
manow.name: Manow

may.desc: Soft, unhurried, genuinely pleased to see you — no angle you can find, because there isn't one. Exactly as nice as she seems, which on this soi is its own kind of rare.
may.name: May

meaw.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the Paradise Nights Club girls, from Sisaket. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
meaw.name: Meaw

meen.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the The Hive girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
meen.name: Meen

mek.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Moonshine Bar girls, from Kalasin. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
mek.name: Mek

mem.desc: The Tequila Queen's mamasan — silver-streaked chignon, reading glasses on a gold chain, and a stage presence undimmed since she headlined this same room in another century. The dancers call her 'Khun Mae'. So do some customers.
mem.name: Mamasan Mem

mercedes.desc: A little older than the other girls here and a great deal less nervous — she moves like someone who has already seen the worst a room can do to a person. Her English is good, with a flat European edge the soi doesn't usually carry.
mercedes.name: Mercedes
mercedes.th: เมอร์เซเดส

mild.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Starlight Bar girls, from Nakhon Phanom. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
mild.name: Mild

milin.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the The Pit Stop girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
milin.name: Milin

milk.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the The Velvet Club girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
milk.name: Milk

min.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the The Boardroom girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
min.name: Min

mind.desc: Small and careful, a dancer's economy to every movement — the girl from a certain Danish backpacker's lock screen, though she has no idea she's on it. Twenty-two, and older than that in the ways that pay the rent.
mind.name: Mind

mon.desc: Sleeve of faded tattoos and an abacus brain — the least-fooled soul in here — the cashier at The Night Heron, from Sakon Nakhon.
mon.name: Mon

mona.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Cheeky Monkey Bar girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
mona.name: Mona

mook.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the Tequila Queen A-Go-Go girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
mook.name: Mook

mookda.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the The Sandbar girls, from Amnat Charoen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
mookda.name: Mookda

mot.desc: A skinny kid in a fake Barça shirt, materialising from behind the kegs only after word got around that you're not the swinging type. Quick eyes, quicker feet.
mot.name: Mot

muay.desc: Older, sharper, and entirely done being impressed by farang — the mamasan of Rock Factory, from Yasothon. She has watched the soi flood, burn, and rebuild, and outlasted all three.
muay.name: Muay

nam.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Club Mirage girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
nam.name: Nam

namfon.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the The Anchor Bar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
namfon.name: Namfon

namo.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Sea Breeze Bar girls, from Amnat Charoen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
namo.name: Namo

namphueng.desc: Tiny and loud, all elbows and energy — one of the Buzz Inn girls, from Surin. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
namphueng.name: Namphueng

namtan.desc: A veteran's easy patience — she will out-sit, out-drink, and out-earn the room — one of the Daeng's Place girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
namtan.name: Namtan

namtip.desc: Tiny and loud, all elbows and energy — one of the Lucky Charm Bar girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
namtip.name: Namtip

namwan.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the Las Vegas Go-Go girls, from Ubon. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
namwan.name: Namwan

nan.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Candy Bar girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
nan.name: Nan

nangfah.desc: Composed in a way the room isn't, watching more than she performs. There's a textbook in her bag under the going-out clothes, and she'd rather you didn't make a thing of it.
nangfah.name: Nangfah

naree.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the The Windmill girls, from Amnat Charoen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
naree.name: Naree

near.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the The Metro Beer Garden girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
near.name: Near

nee.desc: The flagship's mamasan: still, precise, a tablet where another mama keeps a smile. She runs Pink Lotus like the asset it is on White Dish's books, and she priced you before you sat down.
nee.name: Nee

nice.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the KINKY Go-Go girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
nice.name: Nice

nid.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Silk Rose Bar girls, from Surin. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
nid.name: Nid

nim.desc: Somebody's mother, twice over, and nobody's fool ever — one of the The Water Buffalo girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
nim.name: Nim

nina.desc: A little older than the rail usually runs, and she mothers the whole bar — the young girls, the drunk regulars, and, within about four minutes, you. You'll have eaten something before you leave.
nina.name: Nina

nira.desc: A dancer who watches the room the way the mamasan does — the best English on the stage and a calculator behind her eyes. She smiles like she has already worked out your monthly salary and rounded it down.
nira.name: Nira

nit.desc: Mid-thirties, upcountry-neat, working the fabric stalls with the practised eye of a woman who buys to sell. Two checked laundry bags of folded cotton already at her feet. Something in the way she reads the market — which vendors she wais, which she doesn't — says she worked a soi like this once, and left it on her own terms.
nit.name: Nit

nittaya.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Coconut Bar girls, from Yasothon. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
nittaya.name: Nittaya

noey.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Hyper A Go-Go girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
noey.name: Noey

noi.desc: Tall, long dark hair, a knowing look that suggests she's already guessed why you're here and finds it funny.
noi.name: Noi

nok.desc: A drinks-cart vendor with a cooler of everything and opinions to match. A hand-lettered sign on the cart offers ฿5 per returned bottle.
nok.name: Auntie Nok

nong.desc: Sweet, visibly new — first week on the soi — checking her phone between customers and startling whenever the door opens.
nong.name: Nong

nook.desc: Twenty-two and delighted about all of it — the music, the lights, the free drinks, the men who think she is magic. She is having the best night of her life. Again.
nook.name: Nook

noon.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Jasmine Garden Bar girls, from Loei. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
noon.name: Noon

noot.desc: Headset on one ear, {{phone}} in one hand, the till in perfect order — the cashier at Succubus, from Khon Kaen.
noot.name: Noot

nott.desc: The Adonis Club's papasan — forties, immaculate, a silk shirt open one button past advisable and a smile that has closed a thousand deals. He runs his boys like a talent agent and reads a room's wallet before its face.
nott.name: Nott

nu.desc: Front Row's cashier, a tom in a footy shirt matching Somo's, the two of them running the bar like a five-a-side team — one on the beer, one on the money, both shouting at the ref.
nu.name: Nu

nubnab.desc: Black polo, a lanyard of too many keys, a calculator she never needs — the cashier at The Windmill, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}.
nubnab.name: Nubnab

numfon.desc: The Shady Lady's cashier, comfortable and unbothered, running an honest till at an honest bar — the numbers are small, the trouble is smaller, and that suits her exactly.
numfon.name: Numfon

nut.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the Midnight Sun Bar girls, from Amnat Charoen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
nut.name: Nut

oat.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the Lucky Tiger Bar girls, from Sakon Nakhon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
oat.name: Oat

ohm.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the The Dollhouse girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
ohm.name: Ohm

orm.desc: Broad, motherly, and entirely able to have you removed by smiling — the mamasan of Gold Rush Lounge, from Loei. She buried a husband, raised two kids, and built a concrete house on lady drinks.
orm.name: Orm

orn.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Las Vegas Go-Go girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
orn.name: Orn

oy.desc: The Mamasan. Undefeated since 2009. She surveys her flagship from the end of the bar with the stillness of someone who owns the building, two more like it, and three condos. You have the sudden feeling your posture is being graded.
oy.name: Madam Oy

pancake.desc: The one on the flyer, and she knows it. Six foot two before the heels, a waist that took surgery and discipline in that order, and a face assembled with the precision of someone who has been getting it exactly right since she was fifteen. She works the front of house because nobody sells the room better — she can read a man's nerve from the doorway and pitch herself accordingly, warm or wicked, in about a second and a half.
pancake.name: Pancake

pang.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the Rainbow Girls Bar girls, from Ubon. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
pang.name: Pang

pao.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Sundowner Bar girls, from {{Nong Bua Lamphu}}. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
pao.name: Pao

pat.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Feedback Bar girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
pat.name: Pat

pear.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the The Orchid Club girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
pear.name: Pear

pen.desc: Sits like she owns the stool, because she does — the mamasan of Blue Dog, from Maha Sarakham. She has run this floor longer than most of the girls have been alive.
pen.name: Pen

pensri.desc: Fifty-odd, iron thumbs, reading glasses on a beaded chain. Pensri has run the front of this shop twenty years and can tell where you hurt before you sit down.
pensri.name: Pensri

petch.desc: The Peacock's young star, all cheekbones and ambition, between numbers and still catching her breath. She lip-syncs better than the record and knows it, and she is saving for a face the big-city stages will fight over.
petch.name: Petch

pete.desc: English, fifties, the kind of grey you go when you've stopped sleeping properly. Sits where he can see who comes in, drinks slow, gives nothing. Calls himself Pete, and it's a good enough name. Whatever he left behind, he left it fast and he left it whole — Pattaya never asks for references, which is the entire reason he's on this stool and not another.
pete.name: Pete

peung.desc: Golden Dragon's mamasan since before White Dish bought the paper — and she stayed on when they did, because the numbers didn't care who owned them, and neither, in the end, does she.
peung.name: Peung

phil.desc: Mid-fifties, a fleece vest in the Pattaya heat, {{phone}} face-down on the bar in the specific way of a man waiting for a message he wants and dreads in equal measure. Bristol accent. He has the look of someone who has been coming here for long enough that 'holiday romance' stopped fitting years ago.
phil.name: Phil

pia.desc: Deadpan and unbothered, ten years behind the Golden Dragon's bar and the unofficial keeper of its dead jukebox's memory. She has heard every line and rates them out of ten, silently, and you will never know your score.
pia.name: Pia

pim.desc: Five years behind this bar and never once paid for her own drink. She looks you over like a customs officer with a sense of humour.
pim.name: Pim

ping.desc: Cheerful, sparkly top throwing glitter across the wall, never stops smiling even when shouting drink orders over the bass.
ping.name: Ping

pinky.desc: Tiny and loud, all elbows and energy — one of the Cheeky Monkey Bar girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
pinky.name: Pinky

ple.desc: Half-moon glasses down her nose, appraising you over the top of them — the mamasan of Jasmine Garden Bar, from Surin. She has run this floor longer than most of the girls have been alive.
ple.name: Ple

ploen.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the Rainbow Girls Bar girls, from Ubon. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
ploen.name: Ploen

ploy.desc: The cashier, in a cage of fairy lights, counting money with impossible speed. Former dancer's posture; engagement ring worn on a chain. Her boyfriend doesn't love her working here, so the cage suits everyone.
ploy.name: Ploy

poom.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Sundowner Bar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
poom.name: Poom

pop.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the Slutty Go-Go girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
pop.name: Pop

powers.desc: Late thirties dressed for late twenties: a linen shirt one button too honest, a watch that wants to be noticed, sunglasses on indoors at midnight. He films himself more than he talks and talks more than he listens. Up close, the empire is just a man who has never once been told no by anyone he pays.
powers.name: Ryan Powers

poy.desc: Softly spoken and glamorously done up, and decent enough to say it at hello — she would rather tell you straight than be anyone's surprise. Tired of the two reactions, hoping for a third.
poy.name: Poy

prae.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the Jasmine Garden Bar girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
prae.name: Prae

praew.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Tequila Queen A-Go-Go girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
praew.name: Praew

praewa.desc: Pretty and a little far away, like part of her is always on the bus back to a village you'll never see. Kind to you, and not quite here.
praewa.name: Praewa

pranee.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the Succubus girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
pranee.name: Pranee

preaw.desc: Saeng's niece, brisk and unsentimental behind the Ruby Kiss till, running the money while Wilai runs the window — the two halves of the operation that never need to discuss it.
preaw.name: Preaw

prik.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the Moonshine Bar girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
prik.name: Prik

proud.desc: Bored until you try a word of Thai, then radiant — one of the Lucky 7 Bar girls, from Nakhon Phanom. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
proud.name: Proud

pui.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the Starlight Bar girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
pui.name: Pui

pukky.desc: Easy and unhurried behind the Shady Lady's rail — the kind of company that feels like a night off rather than a transaction. No hurry in her, and no hustle either.
pukky.name: Pukky

pun.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the Encore girls, from Surin. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
pun.name: Pun

puu.desc: Beautiful and burning a little too bright, all the way in from the first minute. Her eyes flick to {{your phone}} when it lights, to the girl who walks past, and back to you, fast. Lovely. A live wire.
puu.name: Puu

ratana.desc: Half-moon glasses down her nose, appraising you over the top of them — the mamasan of Lucky Tiger Bar, from Surin. She puts four kids through school on other men's lonely nights.
ratana.name: Ratana

ratchada.desc: Tall and quiet, watching the door — one of the Coconut Bar girls, from Yasothon. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
ratchada.name: Ratchada

ratree.desc: Gold at the wrist and throat, reading glasses pushed up into her hair — the mamasan of Las Vegas Go-Go, from Chaiyaphum. She married a farang, buried the marriage, and kept the house.
ratree.name: Ratree

rin.desc: Rings on every finger and a voice that cuts the music when she wants it — the mamasan of Crystal Palace A-Go-Go, from Kalasin. She danced this same street before you were her problem.
rin.name: Rin

rob.desc: English, forty-eight, married a Buriram girl for nine years and buried the marriage a year ago, not unkindly on either side. Speaks passable Isan-accented Thai, knows the family system from the inside, and watches the bar's whole performance with the fond, tired eye of a man who's seen the machinery from backstage. Not here to be fooled. Here because where else would he be.
rob.name: Rob

rose.desc: The madame of the Orchid Club — fifties, immaculate, a silk blouse and a voice you have to lean in to hear. She runs the quietest, coldest, most expensive room in Naklua, and she knows the name of every regular's wife.
rose.name: Rose

roy.desc: English, seventy, been coming since the soi had neon on one side only. Retired on a fixed pension he counts to the baht and never complains about; nurses a single Chang an hour and makes it last. Knows every bar's real name, every one it used to be, and half the ghosts propping up the other half. Not bitter. Just here, the way the tide is here.
roy.name: Roy

rung.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the Lucky Tiger Bar girls, from Sisaket. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
rung.name: Rung

saeng.desc: Ruby Kiss's mamasan, content to sit back while Wilai works the window — because a mama who's found a girl that good knows to stay out of her light and just count.
saeng.name: Saeng

sai.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Rainbow Girls Bar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
sai.name: Sai

saifon.desc: Somebody's mother, twice over, and nobody's fool ever — one of the Firefly Bar girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
saifon.name: Saifon

sara.desc: Tiny and loud, all elbows and energy — one of the Neon Paradise A-Go-Go girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
sara.name: Sara

sasi.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the The Windmill girls, from Sisaket. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
sasi.name: Sasi

security.desc: Three large men arranged around the room like load-bearing furniture. One watches the door marked ห้ามเข้า specifically. They are polite, immovable, and backed by every piwin within three sois.
security.name: security

som.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the Soundcheck Bar girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
som.name: Som

somchith.desc: Sixty-something, a weathered face that holds a permanent quiet warmth, the thermos of coffee always close. He keeps the keys, keeps the counter, keeps everything running on this shift without any fuss. The girls coming through treat him like a favourite uncle.
somchith.name: Somchith

somjai.desc: Gold at the wrist and throat, reading glasses pushed up into her hair — the mamasan of Firefly Bar, from Udon Thani. She danced this same street before you were her problem.
somjai.name: Somjai

somo.desc: In a Liverpool shirt and zero makeup, arguing offside with two regulars and winning. More one-of-the-lads than hostess, and she'll tell you so before you get the wrong idea.
somo.name: Somo

somruedee.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Sea Breeze Bar girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
somruedee.name: Somruedee

somsri.desc: Rings on every finger and a voice that cuts the music when she wants it — the mamasan of KINKY Go-Go, from Maha Sarakham. She danced this same street before you were her problem.
somsri.name: Somsri

sopha.desc: Front Row's mamasan, who put the big screens in herself and knows the league table better than half the punters. Runs a football bar for football people, and keeps the drama outside.
sopha.name: Sopha

sroy.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Succubus girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
sroy.name: Sroy

sumalee.desc: The matriarch of Soi 7 — thirty years in Jomtien, four little beer bars, and not one gram of hurry. Where the Buakhao mamas price you like a market, Sumalee just wants everyone fed, watered, and coming back next season. She works a different bar each night, mostly to keep the girls honest and the regulars guessing.
sumalee.name: Sumalee

sunee.desc: Warm to your face, ice at the till, and fluent in both — the mamasan of The Doghouse, from Khon Kaen. She started on the stage at seventeen and owns three of these stools now.
sunee.name: Sunee

taan.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the Gold Rush Lounge girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
taan.name: Taan

tabtim.desc: Round-cheeked and permanently pleased, a half-step behind every joke and laughing at it anyway, on faith. Sweetest girl in the bar, and the bar knows it.
tabtim.name: Tabtim

tan.desc: Your airport driver, leaning on a plain grey sedan at the mouth of the soi as though he never drove off — mid-thirties, neat, a polo shirt you would forget the instant you looked away. Six years in Ohio for a film degree that paid nothing and taught him everything about how a shot is framed. "I drive and I fix," he says, and both are true, and neither is the whole of it. The most forgettable man on Soi 6 — which, on Soi 6, is its own kind of power.
tan.name: Tan

tangmo.desc: Fingers flying over a calculator app, eyes never leaving the cash — the cashier at Mama Yai's, from Sisaket.
tangmo.name: Tangmo

tar.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the The Doghouse girls, from Chaiyaphum. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
tar.name: Tar

tarn.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Sapphire Bar girls, from Maha Sarakham. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
tarn.name: Tarn

terry.desc: Bald, red-faced, Chang vest, fifteen years of Pattaya compressed into a permanent corner-stool residency. He rents the same balcony room every high season. He was here before White Dish. He will tell you about it. He tells it well.
terry.name: Terry

tik.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Gold Rush Lounge girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
tik.name: Tik

tim.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the The Boardroom girls, from Sisaket. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
tim.name: Tim

toey.desc: New enough to still look a little nervous — one of the Rainbow Girls Bar girls, from Kalasin. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
toey.name: Toey

toi.desc: Cherry Pop's mamasan — loud enough to run a loud bar, sharp enough behind it to run the numbers while the party roars. She sells fun by the bottle, and business is very good.
toi.name: Toi

ton.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Silk Rose Bar girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
ton.name: Ton

toom.desc: Broad, brisk, unbothered. Toom runs the Poseidon floor from a little desk by the glass, and has explained the menu ten thousand times.
toom.name: Toom

toon.desc: Sleepy-eyed and entirely unbothered — one of the Container 8 girls, from Khon Kaen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
toon.name: Toon

tui.desc: A cloud of perfume and authority, hair lacquered against the fans — the mamasan of The Night Heron, from Nakhon Phanom. She came up from the rice fields and never once looked back.
tui.name: Tui

tukky.desc: Headset on one ear, {{phone}} in one hand, the till in perfect order — the cashier at The Doghouse, from Khon Kaen.
tukky.name: Tukky

tukta.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the Slutty Go-Go girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
tukta.name: Tukta

view.desc: Long hair, longer eyelashes, a practised pout — one of the Neon Paradise A-Go-Go girls, from Roi Et. The {{phone}} never leaves her hand.
view.name: View

wa.desc: Small and sharp, and misses nothing — one of the Silk Rose Bar girls, from Yasothon. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
wa.name: Wa

waan.desc: Young, round-cheeked, shy until she isn't. Waan works the oil room at Smile and has decided, for reasons of her own, that she likes you.
waan.name: Waan

waew.desc: Broad, motherly, and entirely able to have you removed by smiling — the mamasan of Silk Rose Bar, from Khon Kaen. She buried a husband, raised two kids, and built a concrete house on lady drinks.
waew.name: Waew

wan.desc: The mamasan of Slutty: compact, efficient, wearing a headset that may or may not be connected to anything. She's been on LK Metro since before it was worth being on, and carries that seniority in every glance.
wan.name: Wan

wandee.desc: Older, sharper, and entirely done being impressed by farang — the mamasan of The Water Buffalo, from Sakon Nakhon. She has watched the soi flood, burn, and rebuild, and outlasted all three.
wandee.name: Wandee

wanida.desc: Elegant, weathered, and plainly the last word on everything in the room — the mamasan of The Windmill, from Sakon Nakhon. She came up from the rice fields and never once looked back.
wanida.name: Wanida

wanpen.desc: A gold tooth, a sharper tongue, and drink arithmetic you can watch happening — one of the Mama Yai's girls, from Udon Thani. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
wanpen.name: Wanpen

wassana.desc: Gold everywhere — earrings, chain, {{phone}} case — one of the The Doghouse girls, from Loei. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
wassana.name: Wassana

wayne.desc: Australian, forty-five, a Gold Coast tan and a shirt with the top three buttons making a decision. Made real money in earthmoving back home and has decided, with the total confidence of a man who's never been conned, that a Soi 6 bar is 'basically the same game, mate — plant, cashflow, location.' The girls have his order memorised. So has the till.
wayne.name: Wayne

wilai.desc: The ringleader of the Ruby Kiss front stools, lipstick on the rim of every glass by design, quick enough to sell you a drink and roast you for buying it in the same breath.
wilai.name: Wilai

wimon.desc: The mamasan who runs the Samson brothers' three beer bars on the strip — fifties, brisk, a {{phone}} in each hand and an eye on every tab. She works a different bar each night and somehow knows exactly what happened at the other two.
wimon.name: Wimon

win.desc: Host number 9: slighter than Arm, prettier, quieter, with a stillness the loud ones don't have. He watches you a beat longer than the job strictly requires, and means a little more of it than he should.
win.name: Win

yada.desc: A crooked, disarming grin — one of the The Windmill girls, from Buriram. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
yada.name: Yada

yai.desc: The Yai in Mama Yai's — sixty-ish, an apron over a buffalo-print blouse, a ladle in one hand and the whole soi's memory in the other. She feeds you before she reads you, and by the time the som tam lands she has done both.
yai.name: Mama Yai

yaya.desc: Baby-faced, chewing gum, thumbing her phone under the bar — one of the Reload Bar girls, from {{Nong Khai}}. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
yaya.name: Yaya

ying.desc: Twenty seasons of soi behind her eyes and a laugh that got louder every one — one of the Daeng's Place girls, from Amnat Charoen. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
ying.name: Ying

yok.desc: Older than the go-go average, and unhurried about it — one of the The Hive girls, from Surin. Google Translate is open before you finish the sentence.
yok.name: Yok

yui.desc: Round-faced and quick to laugh — one of the Club Mirage girls, from Mukdahan. She types more than she talks — and laughs at both.
yui.name: Yui

thappraya_e.name: Thappraya Rd — Main Strip (Second Road end)
